Title: Module 2 - Sync Data from ATS to LinkedIn

Blocks.Section: Module 2 - Sync Data from ATS to LinkedIn
Blocks.Text: As a LinkedIn partner, you must sync your customers' ATS data to LinkedIn to support their recruiting workflows. Module 2 covers creating and updating records, syncing historical data, and verifying data completeness and quality. To complete Module 2 certification, demonstrate each applicable test case below to LinkedIn.

Blocks.Text: Three checks are identical across every entity: entity ID fidelity, ingestion latency against source timestamps, and completeness. To keep the tables readable, each one is stated once in Cross-cutting as RSC-210-004, RSC-210-006, and RSC-210-005, with a per-entity lookup table, rather than repeated in every section. Referential integrity stays per entity, because the parent key it validates differs by entity.

Blocks.Section: Module 2 - Sync Data from ATS to LinkedIn
Blocks.Text: Applicant evaluation, which covers retrieving evaluations, is certified in Module 3 alongside the other retrieval surfaces.

Map your candidate data model (certification prerequisite)1. Produce a field-level mapping of your ATS candidate model → the LinkedIn candidate schema (externalCandidateId, firstName, lastName, emailAddresses, phoneNumbers, currentCompanyName, currentJobTitle, linkedInProfileUrl, sources and other fields).

Share a mapping between your ATS candidate data model and the LinkedIn candidate schema (for example, externalCandidateId, firstName, lastName, emailAddresses, phoneNumbers, currentCompanyName, currentJobTitle, linkedInProfileUrl, sources and other fields). This mapping is a certification prerequisite used for testing and data-analysis work by LinkedIn.

Create a new candidate1. Create a new candidate in the ATS with unique values for all fields.2. For the candidate that was synced, find the matched profile in Recruiter search results and profile page, and confirm the unique values appear in the In-ATS indicator.3. Demonstrate that the correct LinkedIn profile appears in the ATS Profile Widget.4. Confirm you get and store the person URN with retry and exponential backoff implemented (share a code snippet or code snapshot).5. Ensure all in-scope fields are synced — the required fields plus the optional fields in scope (refer to field-scope notes).

• The unique values for all synced fields appear in the In-ATS indicator in Recruiter search results and the profile page of the matched candidate.• The correct LinkedIn profile appears in the ATS Profile Widget.• The partner stores the person URN in their ATS.• No error is observed in the LinkedIn API access log.• Any field not being received at LinkedIn is noted and flagged for approval.Related documentation: Profile Plugin

Update a candidate1. Edit the value of a synced field (FirstName or LastName or PhoneNumber) in your ATS for the previously created candidate.2. Find the candidate that was updated on LinkedIn Recruiter. From the In-ATS Indicator and from the ATS tab, check that the changed value is displayed there.

• The new value is reflected in the In-ATS indicator or ATS on the Recruiter profile page of the synced candidate and in search results.• ATS updates are reflected in LinkedIn in real-time (or within your stated sync frequency if not real-time).

Verify private or anonymous candidate handling1. For a private or anonymous candidate on an active integration, send the candidate and application with all identifying information scrubbed.2. Confirm no resume or attachment is sent for this candidate — neither during the initial historical sync nor during any ongoing or real-time sync (that is, at no point).

• For a private or anonymous candidate on an active integration, ensure you send the candidate and application with all identifying information scrubbed.• Ensure the scrubbed candidate or application data does not appear anywhere in the LinkedIn system.• Ensure you correctly honor the privacy requirements for private and anonymous candidates.• Resumes and attachments must never be sent for private or anonymous candidates — this exclusion applies both to the initial historical sync and to all subsequent syncs. For every other (non-private) candidate, resumes or attachments are synced normally at all times (validated in the Resumes section).Related documentation: Sync Documents
Sync historical candidate data1. Sync historical candidates from your ATS to LinkedIn.

• On LinkedIn Recruiter, ensure that all synced candidates are available with the In-ATS indicator.• On the ATS, in the ATS Profile Widget, ensure that the correct LinkedIn profile appears for a candidate.• Ensure all the candidates are synced from the beginning for the corresponding customer.

Verify candidate referential integrity1. For a sample of candidates, show each externalCandidateId is unique and non-fabricated (refer to Entity ID Fidelity, RSC-210-004).2. Where multiple source records collapse into one candidate, show the parent candidate's ID is used consistently across all child applications or attachments or candidate notes.3. Share the code or payload showing how externalCandidateId is populated and how collapses are resolved.

• Candidate is a top-level entity and has no parent ATS reference, so referential integrity here means externalCandidateId is stable, unique and non-fabricated.• Every child entity (application, attachment, candidate note) that references this candidate must use the same externalCandidateId.• No child entity may reference a candidate id that was never synced.

Share a mapping between your ATS attachment data model and the LinkedIn attachment schema. This mapping is a certification prerequisite used for testing and data-analysis work by LinkedIn.
Create a candidate application resume1. Create a new application resume in the ATS and sync it.

• Ensure the new application resume appears in the Attachments tab or the In-ATS tab for a given candidate in LinkedIn Recruiter.• [For ATS Connected Projects]: In LinkedIn Recruiter, ensure the new application resume appears in the Attachments and In-ATS tab for an Applicant within an ATS Connected Project.
Sync historical application resume data1. Sync all application resumes.

• Ensure all application resumes are synced from your ATS to LinkedIn.• Ensure all the historical application resumes are synced.• In LinkedIn Recruiter, ensure all synced application resumes are available through the Attachments tab, the In-ATS tab, or both.• [For ATS Connected Projects]: In LinkedIn Recruiter, ensure all synced application resumes are available in applications within associated ATS Connected Projects (link the attachment or resume to the application id).

Verify resume or attachment referential integrity1. For a sample of application resumes, show each record's externalReferenceEntityId resolves to a valid, already-synced application.2. Share the code or payload showing how externalReferenceEntityId is populated.

• Every application resume must be linked to a valid, synced application through externalReferenceEntityId.• No application resume may reference a missing, invalid, or fabricated application id.• Orphaned application resumes (no valid parent) must be surfaced as a data-quality issue (refer to the Resume or attachment DQ check).
Sync historical application resume data1. Compare the total resume count on your side vs LinkedIn.2. The LinkedIn team will share the count of records present in LinkedIn.

The total number of resumes in the ATS should match the count in LinkedIn.(quantitative check: the count of application resumes from your side for the loaded customer test tenant is validated against the count of resumes synced at LinkedIn.)A variance of up to 5% between your side and LinkedIn counts is tolerable.

Sync historical application resume dataUse the loaded customer test tenant.1. Produce the resume DQ report and confirm < 10% of applications cannot be associated with a Resume.2. The LinkedIn team will share the data quality report for the records present in LinkedIn.
Ensure the following data quality requirement is met:• < 10% of applications cannot be associated with a Resume (looking at both application and candidate resumes, if available)

Verify historical resume or attachment data quality1. The LinkedIn team will share the data quality report for the records synced during loaded test tenant sync and during historical sync in LinkedIn.
• Ensure that the data quality requirement is matched.• If any schema field of the Resume or attachment schema is not mapped or synced, mention the same.

Sync historical application resume data1. Once functional, quantitative, and qualitative pass, re-run the same historical sync functional, quantitative, and qualitative checks on the charter customer tenant(s).2. Obtain sign-off from the product managers and the RSC or CRM Connect team.3. This is a LinkedIn internal checklist item.

Once the functional, quantitative, and qualitative checks pass, you are ready for beta. Re-run the same historical sync functional, quantitative, and qualitative checks on the charter customer tenant(s).

These test cases apply across all entities in Module 2. Three of them —
Entity ID Fidelity (RSC-210-004), Completeness or Filters or Mandatory Fields
(RSC-210-005), and Ingestion Latency vs Source Timestamps (RSC-210-006) —
consolidate checks that were previously repeated per entity; each has a per-entity lookup
table immediately below the main table.

Rows.Text: Push the full historical dataset on re-activation1. Push the customer's complete historical data (not a subset).2. De-activate then re-activate the integration.3. On re-activation, show a full historical backfill and that the same child developerApplication is reused (no new application is created).

• You must push the customer's complete historical data rather than a partial subset.• A full historical push is also required whenever a customer re-activates the integration after a prior de-activation.• On re-activation, a full historical backfill occurs and the same child developerApplication is reused. A new one must not be created, as described in RSC-101-007.
Verify idempotency and prevent duplicates1. Re-send an already-synced entity (candidate, application, requisition, stage, or resume) using the same external ID.

• Re-send an already-synced entity (candidate, application, job requisition, stage, or resume) using the same external ID.• LinkedIn must upsert the existing record — it must not create a second copy.• This complements Entity ID Fidelity: stable, one-to-one external IDs are what make idempotent upserts possible.

Handle errors and track 4XX or 5XX responses1. State whether your ATS allows data syncing with missing required fields during historical or regular sync. If it does, show how errors are handled and surfaced to the customer, and how the customer fixes them.2. Demonstrate this through a historical sync using erroneous data, and through the ATS UI.3. For 4XX and 5XX, describe the retry logic through a code snippet or a written explanation.4. Provide a call-and-response log, including response headers, that is stored in your ATS.5. For a batch request that fails while returning 200, log the full failure, including request and response bodies and headers, with an example screenshot.6. Track the 4XX and 5XX count or rate, especially during the charter phase, and review it at beta-exit.

• Sync data with missing required fields and show how data errors are handled and surfaced to the customer, and how the customer fixes them.• For unexpected errors (4XX and 5XX), describe the retry logic and logging used to identify and report issues; provide a call-and-response log (including response headers) for debugging customer-support issues.• If any request in a batch fails even when the HTTP response is 200, log the failure for the entire request (request body, headers, response headers, response body) with an example link.• Track the count or rate of 4XX and 5XX responses you receive — especially during the charter phase — and review it as part of beta-exit sign-off.Related documentation: Error Handling

Verify entity ID fidelity for all entities1. For each synced entity, show its external ID (and any parent IDs) equals the ID returned by your own API — strict 1:1, no fabricated IDs, no added prefix or suffix. See the Entity ID Fidelity table below for the field(s) per entity.2. Where multiple source records collapse into one, use the top-level (parent) record's ID.3. Share a code block or API signature or sample payload showing where each ID is sourced.

• Each entity's external ID is identical to the ID returned if we called your own API directly (strict one-to-one mapping).• Fabricated or generated IDs are not allowed, and no added prefix or suffix is permitted (for job requisitions, the human-readable vanityIdentifier is distinct from the canonical externalJobRequisitionId).• On record collapse, the parent record's ID is used consistently across all child entities.• Verification (code review): Calling your own internal API to diff IDs is out of scope for RSC API verification — LinkedIn confirms the mapping through the shared code or payload. See the per-entity ID table below.

Verify sync completeness, filters, and mandatory fields for all entities1. For each synced entity, compare source-vs-LinkedIn record counts for the full historical window (from the beginning of time) to confirm none are dropped.2. Disclose any record types that are intentionally not synced, and any filters applied.3. Confirm your records carry all mandatory fields the corresponding LinkedIn entity requires. See the Completeness scope table below.

• Per-entity record counts match between source and LinkedIn (allowing only the declared exclusions or filters); all record types for every entity are synced.• Any excluded record types or applied filters are explicitly noted.• Mandatory fields required by each LinkedIn entity are present. See the entities-in-scope table below.

Compare ingestion latency against source timestamps for all entities1. For each synced entity, measure the delta between your source create or modify timestamps and LinkedIn ingestion time. See the Ingestion Latency table below for the timestamp fields per entity.2. The LinkedIn team will share the delta report for the records present in LinkedIn.

The per-entity delta stays within the expected ingestion SLA of 5–30 minutes (near-real-time sync). A delta consistently beyond 30 minutes must be justified and discussed with the LinkedIn team. See the per-entity timestamp table below.

Re-run note and interview feedback checks during the charter phase1. Once the functional, quantitative, and qualitative checks pass for application notes, application interview feedback and Candidate Notes, re-run those same checks on the charter customer tenant(s).2. Obtain sign-off from the product managers and the RSC or CRM Connect team.3. This is a LinkedIn internal checklist item.

Once the functional, quantitative, and qualitative checks pass for these lower-priority note or feedback entities, re-run them on the charter customer tenant(s). Charter-phase metrics must be reviewed and signed off by the product managers and the RSC or CRM Connect team before certification (GA). (All other entities carry their own per-entity Charter row.)
